correctness.rationale: For F_h(u)=u-h(I+11^T)sin u and h<1, subtracting coordinates of an inverse of a diagonal target reduces to q_h(ui)=q_h(uj) modulo 2pi; q_h(v)=v-h sin v is a degree-one circle diffeomorphism, forcing all coordinates equal. Thus all backward ancestors reduce to f_c(u)=u-c sin u, c=(d+1)h. For 1<c<2, its critical points ±acos(1/c) give a three-branch window |t|<a_c=sqrt(c²-1)-acos(1/c), and each outer branch is one-to-one forever. Target zero generates ± one new outer ancestor per level, N_n(0)=2n+1. Nonzero central inverse grows in magnitude at least by (c-1)^(-1), so eventually exits; Taylor expansion of f_c near zero plus summable O(u_j²) distortion yields 2 log(1/|t|)/log(1/(c-1))+O_c(1) eventual count. Independent numerical bracketing gave N_n(0)=1,3,5,7,9,11 for c=1.2,1.5,1.9 at n=0..5 and finite stabilization for off-zero examples; numerical tolerance cannot certify the asymptotic.
